title: Map interaction fallbacks and ARIA state machine for embedded controls
creator: Marissa Chen
description: Audit and formalize a predictable interaction fallback model and an ARIA state-machine for small, embedded controls (inline editors, chips, mini-chart toolbars, row actions). These components frequently lose keyboard focus or present inconsistent screen reader semantics when used inside virtualized lists and dense tables. Goal: reduce keyboard traps, make focus handoff deterministic, and produce a repeatable evidence package for accessibility reviewers and VPAT needs.
tasks: Inventory: compile a canonical list of embedded controls across the component library (chip, inline-edit, mini-chart toolbar, row-action menu, table-cell editor). Link artifacts.
Prototype: create an ARIA state-machine diagram illustrating states (idle, focusable, active-edit, nested-popup, escaped) and transition rules with example DOM patterns.
Spec: write updated component contracts describing tabindex, role, aria-expanded, aria-controls, and recommended keyboard sequences for focus handoff.
Implement prototypes in Storybook for 3 components (chips, inline-edit, row-action) demonstrating handoff in virtualized lists.
Test: run manual screen reader passes (NVDA, VoiceOver) and keyboard-only flows; capture audio/video evidence and issue remediation tickets for failing patterns.
Documentation: assemble playbook section with do/don't examples, recommended utility attributes, and sample A/C for QA teams.
Bundle evidence: prepare VPAT evidence snippets and conformance notes for the audit team.
Review: schedule design + engineering walkthrough and collect signoff; handoff to ENG for rollout and integration tests.
Follow-up: add a CI regression test harness storybook snapshot for focus order and keyboard scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical inventory of embedded controls completed and validated by PM and Eng
State-machine diagram published in Confluence and linked from component docs
Three Storybook prototypes demonstrating deterministic focus handoff in virtualized contexts
Screen reader runs for prototypes recorded with clear remediation tickets for any remaining failures
Playbook published with example HTML snippets, recommended attributes, and QA checkslist
VPAT evidence bundle contains at least one passing example per WCAG 2.1 AA scenario we claim
Engineering has an implementation plan with dependencies and a test matrix for rollout

notes: Avoid global focus management patches; prefer per-component explicit anchors to keep behavior predictable across deployments.
Consider adding a small accessibility util in the design system that exposes a stable handoff API (e.g., registerHandoffAnchor(elementId)).
Coordinate with Runtime/ENG for any changes that might affect event delegation in virtualized lists.
